Janderson? I almost didn't recognize you! It's Lauren, from the New York office.
Lauren! Of course. You used to sit next to the window on the fourth floor.
That's right. And you used to bring that terrible coffee every morning.
I still do, honestly. Do you still live in Brooklyn?
No, I moved away years ago. I didn't use to like the suburbs, but nowadays I love them.
And the commute? You used to hate the subway.
I work from home three days a week now, so I only commute twice. Did you use to work in research?
I did. Back then I used to write reports all day. Nowadays I spend my time with clients.

I grew up in a small town in Ohio, and I go back about once a year. Every time, it feels a little stranger. There used to be a cinema on the main street, and on Friday nights the whole town used to go. It closed when I was fifteen, and nowadays it is a pharmacy. My father used to walk to work in five minutes. Now nobody walks anywhere, because the offices moved to a business park outside town, and everybody commutes by car. I didn't use to notice any of this when I lived there. You only see how much a place has changed when you move away, and then come back as a visitor.

When I started in private banking twenty years ago, things were very different. We used to print every report, and a client used to wait a week for an answer. Most of my clients didn't use to ask about fees. They asked about returns, and that was the whole conversation. Nowadays they read everything on their phones before they call me, and very often the first question is about fees. Back then I used to think my job was to know more than the client. Now I think my job is to explain things better than the internet does. It is harder, but honestly, I would not go back.

Lauren recognizes Janderson and tells him who she is. He remembers where she used to sit in the New York office. She tells him she moved away from Brooklyn years ago. He asks about her commute, and she says she works from home three days a week. Finally, she asks if he used to work in research, and he says he did.
